newsitem.title: UK: Outlook varied for CIS minor metals - Roskill.
newsitem.headline: Outlook varied for CIS minor metals - Roskill.

text.p: Several CIS minor metals may share common problems but the outlook varies widely for each market, a report from market analyst Roskill said.

On indium, Roskill said the main feature of production in the CIS was the low degree of recovery from raw materials. In 1995 only eight tonnes of indium metal were recovered by Russian organisations from domestic copper, zinc, lead, pyrite and tin concentrates which contained around 22 tonnes of indium. This was a recovery rate of only 36 percent.

Financial problems faced by Russian aluminium producers make them unable to invest in gallium production which is of minor importance to them. But Roskill said PAZ in Kazakhstan showed a brighter prospect.

In 1995 PAZ was transferred to White Swan Ltd in trust management. Prior to this PAZ had been unable to sell any of the gallium produced in the previous three years but during 1995 the managing company sold the plant's complete stock of gallium.

Prospects for germanium production in Russia appear good due to the likelihood that mining will restart, availability of processing capacity at the Krastsvetmet plant and strong demand for the metal on world markets, Roskill said.
The majority of Russian output will be exported as domestic consumption will remain low in the short-term.
Roskill added that the future of germanium production in Ukraine looks uncertain.
Russian selenium and tellurium production appears stable but may fall in the short term because of the restructuring of production by RAO Norilsk Nickel, Roskill said.
Output by the Ust-Kamenogorsk combine in Kazakhstan is likely to continue to fall in 1997.
In Uzbekistan an increase in copper mining is possible in the short-term and some increase in selenium and tellurium production is also forecast, it said. --London Newsroom +44 171 542-8075
